papers.title: Risk-aware hybrid reinforcement learning and robust optimization for reliable PV-battery scheduling under uncertainty
papers.abstract: Abstract The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation and battery energy storage systems (BESSs) has intensified the need for intelligent scheduling strategies that can simultaneously reduce operating cost, preserve battery health, and ensure operational reliability under significant uncertainty. In practical grid-connected PV–battery systems, the stochastic nature of solar power, load demand, and electricity prices often leads to constraint violations and high tail-risk costs when conventional optimization or purely data-driven methods are used. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a risk-sensitive hybrid framework that integrates Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), conformal uncertainty estimation (CUE), and robust optimization (RO) in a unified energy management architecture. The SAC agent learns a stochastic dispatch policy, while CVaR explicitly penalizes unfavorable cost outcomes and CUE provides distribution-free uncertainty bounds for uncertain inputs. These bounds are then embedded into a robust optimization layer to guarantee feasibility under adverse operating conditions. In addition, an adaptive fusion mechanism combines the outputs of the learning-based and robust controllers to balance economic performance and reliability. Simulation results for a typical residential PV–battery system demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best trade-off among cost, risk, and constraint satisfaction. Compared with a rule-based baseline, the full model reduces the SOC violation rate from 4.8% to below 1%, while also lowering the total operating cost and CVaR. Moreover, the proposed framework outperforms the RO-only variant by achieving a lower average cost without sacrificing robustness, and it consistently provides the highest reliability across independent runs. These results confirm that the proposed hybrid approach offers a practical and scalable solution for secure and economical PV–battery scheduling under uncertainty.

papers.title: World-model-inspired latent action priors for home energy optimization
papers.abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into residential microgrids introduces operational challenges associated with intermittency, electricity-price volatility, and the progressive degradation of battery storage systems. Reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising approach for battery scheduling, yet many existing methods remain vulnerable to actions that fall outside the support of the training data and often generalize poorly across operating regimes. This work proposes an offline reinforcement learning framework that combines a conditional variational autoencoder with latent action priors in order to constrain policy optimization to a structured latent action space learned from expert demonstrations generated by entropy-regularized and deterministic actor-critic controllers. The proposed methodology consists of three stages: first, learning a latent representation of admissible battery actions from expert trajectories through a conditional variational autoencoder; second, extracting an offline policy within the learned latent manifold through implicit value-based policy improvement; and third, deploying an out-of-distribution detection mechanism that gradually blends the learned controller with a conservative fallback policy under distributional uncertainty. Experiments on the GEFCom2014 benchmark, the StoreNet House 4 scenario, and the CityLearn environment show that the proposed method achieves the highest daily net benefit among value-based and offline controllers, with improvements of up to 61.9% over deep Q-learning and 7.9% over standard model predictive control on GEFCom2014. In addition, the method converges substantially faster than competing baselines, requiring up to nine times less training time in CityLearn. At the same time, the results show that the approach does not uniformly dominate all references: in the policy-based comparison on CityLearn, deep deterministic policy gradients achieve a lower monetary cost, and in standard continuous-control benchmarks, proximal policy optimization and twin delayed deterministic policy gradients outperform the proposed method on specific metrics in selected environments. Ablation studies further show that expert-dataset diversity and rare-event coverage are essential for policy quality, while posterior-collapse diagnostics confirm that the learned latent representation remains informative throughout training. Overall, the proposed framework constitutes a competitive and computationally efficient alternative for offline energy management, particularly in settings where safe exploration, fast convergence, and degradation-aware control are more critical than unconstrained asymptotic performance.

papers.title: Integrating machine learning demand forecasting and adaptive operational control in inpatient stroke care: an analysis with real hospital data
papers.abstract: Objective: To compare capacity allocation policies for inpatient stroke care integrating Random Forest demand forecasting with machine-learning model predictive control (ML-MPC). Methods: Retrospective simulation study using 6,224 stroke admissions at a public neurological reference hospital in Southeastern Brazil (2006–2022). A daily series (2015–2022) was split into training (2015–2019), validation (2020) and test (2021–2022). Base capacity was derived from the 90th percentile of the observed daily census. Six policies were simulated over 727 days, with multi-step forecasts generated recursively from information available at each decision instant; uncertainty was assessed by moving-block bootstrap, re-executing all policies on resampled trajectories. Results: ML-MPC attained a mean simulated queue of 0.55 patients and the lowest objective-function value, 58% below the robust policy using 71% less extraordinary capacity (708 fewer units), and 46% below a naive fixed-capacity policy; 95% intervals excluded zero for blocks of 14, 30 and 60 days. Random Forest accuracy exceeded a historical-mean benchmark only marginally (MAE 0.994 vs 0.999). Conclusion: Within model conditions, how forecasts, uncertainty and capacity constraints entered sequential decisions mattered more than forecast accuracy. Outcomes are simulation estimates; no patient was exposed, the risk term is a non-validated relative index, and objective weights are judgment-based, not monetary.

papers.title: BALANCE-ST: distilling deep reinforcement learning policies into PLC logic for multi-VFD load balancing
papers.abstract: Industrial multi-VFD load balancing on programmable logic controllers (PLCs) requires control policies that are accurate, transparent, and fast enough for deterministic scan cycles. Deep reinforcement learning can learn effective balancing strategies, but neural policies are difficult to inspect and deploy as IEC 61131-3 Structured Text (ST). We propose BALANCE-ST, a simulation-to-PLC pipeline that trains a deep Q -network (DQN) teacher, distils it into a depth-2 decision tree selected by held-out validation parsimony, renders the tree as PLC-oriented ST, and wraps the resulting policy with a deterministic guard enforcing command-bound, ramp-rate, dwell-time, and overload checks. In an in-distribution post-training evaluation across eight demand families and ten seeds, BALANCE-ST achieves mean load-imbalance coefficient of variation 0.0697 versus 0.0696 for the ten-teacher DQN aggregate, while reducing imbalance by \(34.4\%\) , \(52.6\%\) , and \(15.0\%\) relative to equal-share, threshold-staging, and PI baselines, respectively. On the interquartile mean, the reduction versus threshold staging is \(43.2\%\) . A guard ablation and hard-stress evaluation show that the runtime guard reduces realised violations at the cost of higher imbalance under actuator dropout. Compared with beam-search model predictive control, BALANCE-ST yields higher imbalance but much lower online decision cost and a compact policy with four leaves and three effective actions. These results support BALANCE-ST as a practical trade-off between control performance, inspectability, and deployment-oriented simplicity for PLC-based multi-VFD control.

papers.title: Timed Elastic Band based trajectory planning and MPC based adaptive cruise control for car-like autonomous vehicle
papers.abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical control architecture for a car-like autonomous vehicle. Lateral motion is handled by a Timed Elastic Band (TEB) local planner that repeatedly optimizes a short-horizon waypoint band, while steering is generated by a Pure Pursuit controller tracking the optimized local path. Longitudinal behaviour is governed by a model predictive control (MPC) based adaptive cruise control (ACC) that regulates speed and inter-vehicle distance in free-driving and car-following modes, explicitly respecting acceleration and braking limits and enforcing a minimum safety distance. Safety is addressed through constraint-aware planning and control: the TEB optimization penalizes proximity to obstacles and violations of lane boundaries using smooth penalty terms that support stable gradient-based updates, while the MPC-ACC embeds hard bounds and distance constraints to prevent unsafe following. The integrated stack is evaluated in representative driving scenarios, including lane keeping and car-following, and is benchmarked against the MathWorks Path Following Control System (PFCS) reference model to quantify tracking behaviour and constraint compliance under identical conditions.

papers.title: Measuring Coherence in Predictive Models
papers.abstract: Many sequential decision-making procedures, such as active learning, implicitly assume that a model's current predictions agree with those it expects to make after updating on new data, a property we call coherence. Most models in use do not update by exact conditioning and are not guaranteed to be coherent, which can lead to worse decisions. Yet there is currently no general way to measure incoherence or to tell when it matters. We develop tools to measure incoherence and characterise when it affects decisions. We introduce the incoherence ratio, an MMD-based measure of how far any updating procedure departs from coherence, computed only from the procedure's own predictions and updates, and accompany it with an anytime-valid test of coherence. In Bayesian experimental design, acquisition objectives that are equivalent for coherent models choose different data under every approximate model we study, and the incoherence ratio tracks how far incoherence distorts them. We also introduce action coherence, which captures only the incoherence that changes a decision. What a resulting disagreement costs, however, is determined primarily by predictive accuracy. Sequential decisions depend on how a model updates as well as on what it predicts, so coherence, like accuracy, should be checked rather than assumed.

papers.title: DexFormer 2.0: Towards a Cross-Embodiment Foundation Policy for Dexterous Grasping
papers.abstract: Dexterous grasping policies are usually trained for one arm paired with one hand. Every new pairing then needs its own policy, and the number of policies grows with every arm and hand added. We ask whether a single policy can control many arm-hand combinations and transfer to pairings and hands it has never seen. This is hard because robots differ in the number, layout, and dynamics of their joints, so their observations and actions share no common interface. We present DexFormer 2.0, a single reinforcement learning policy for cross-embodiment dexterous grasping. It maps every robot to a canonical joint interface with validity masks, encodes each joint's morphology with attention biased by the kinematic tree, and uses a Transformer-XL memory to infer embodiment-dependent dynamics from recent interaction. Trained on 18 combinations of four arms and six hands, it reaches 89% stable success on seen combinations and 51% on six held-out arm-hand pairs, outperforming GRU and DexFormer 1.0 baselines. Without fine-tuning, it also grasps with four new hand types and, through retargeting, with parallel grippers. Ablations show that memory, the kinematic-tree bias, and broader pairing coverage each matter for transfer. Lido di Venezia is represented as a heterogeneous graph built from public elevation, road, building and census data and driven by hourly tide-gauge records from 1983 to 2024, with seven actions taken from the municipal emergency plan. A PPO policy is trained on this graph and compared, on storm windows unseen in training, with a rule-based system simulating the officer's discretionary decisions. papers.title: Washout-free synchronization, parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification of echo state networks
papers.abstract: Echo state networks (ESNs) forecast chaotic systems for several Lyapunov times. Like all recurrent networks, ESNs require a washout before forecasting, i.e., a phase in which the full state drives the network until the reservoir state synchronizes with the system. At deployment, however, sensors measure only part of the state, with noise and at a lower sampling rate than the training data. We propose a washout-free deployment of ESNs via ensemble data assimilation. In closed loop, the ESN is a Markovian dynamical system; hence, a sequential filter can correct its reservoir state whenever data are available. The filter synchronizes an ensemble of reservoir states, drawn from the training data, with the system, and quantifies the forecast uncertainty. We extend the method to parametric ESNs, to infer physical parameters, and to parallel ESNs with localization, to forecast high-dimensional systems. We test the method on the Lorenz-63 and Lorenz-96 systems. First, the filter synchronizes the ESN with a fraction of the data of a washout. Second, the filter deploys one full-state ESN from a subset of its components, which a washout cannot do. Third, the filter estimates a forcing that is not in the training data, and the estimated forcing lengthens the forecast. Fourth, localization synchronizes a parallel ESN with eight times fewer members than the global filter. Fifth, the ensemble spread signals, without the true state, when the ESN synchronizes and when the filter fails. This work enables the deployment of ESNs from partial, sparse and noisy observations.

papers.abstract: An autonomous vehicle must foresee the consequences of its actions, especially in the rare, time-critical situations where crashes happen. Within this coverage a planner can hardly improve on the data, and beyond it the model's errors mislead it. Logs of competent driving rarely contain the failures that would widen the coverage, and agents that learn from interaction gain them only by failing themselves, without being shown what to do instead. We propose SAFER, a framework that learns offline from failures that others make, judged by an expert, and keeps learning online from its own driving. Offline, partially trained agents and scripted, recoverable perturbations Stage failures in simulation, and an expert Annotates every visited state with its action and value, so that much of what the planner explores is covered before it drives. In planning, a chunked latent world model Foresees the consequences fast enough for real-time use, and a risk-aware sampling-based planner Evaluates candidate maneuvers by their return minus a bounded collision penalty. Online, a loop continuously Refines the model wherever this driving leaves the coverage of the offline data. In closed-loop evaluation against the compared methods, SAFER reaches the highest route completion and reward per step on the CARLA Leaderboard routes, 0.95 and 0.77 from a privileged bird's-eye view, and the highest episode reward in MetaDrive, 53.4 in regular and 49.0 in safety-critical traffic. papers.abstract: Masked modeling is the dominant self-supervised paradigm for point-cloud videos. However, it leaks the information it is meant to predict, whether it reconstructs masked points as in MAE-style methods or predicts their latent features. Because point-cloud tokens are anchored at points sampled from each frame, querying a target at its own position reveals where its geometry has moved, in reconstruction and latent prediction alike. For latent predictors, random spatio-temporal masks introduce a further shortcut, as visible frames on both sides of each target allow interpolation rather than forecasting. The pretext task thus reduces to completion. Once the target positions are withheld, a masked latent predictor performs only slightly better than copying the last frame. To remove this leakage, we propose PointWM, a latent world model that turns completion into forecasting by predicting the features and geometry of future frames from strictly earlier context. Each target is queried only with its last-seen position and timestamp, while a latent action learned without annotations is meant to capture the part of the future that the past leaves undetermined. On HOI4D action segmentation with a P4Transformer backbone, PointWM improves F1@50 over training from scratch by 24.9 offline and 29.1 under strictly causal inference. These results show the promise of latent world models as a leakage-free pretraining paradigm for point-cloud videos.Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/InitalZ/PointWM.

papers.abstract: On-ramp merging is a typical safety and throughput problem on highways. With recent advances in connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), vehicles can be trained to coordinate for safe and efficient merging. However, in dense traffic, forming an effective observation of the traffic state is challenging. For example, observing only the neighbouring vehicles may lead to locally optimal decisions, while observing the entire traffic can introduce much irrelevant information. In this paper, we propose a transformer-based MARL vehicle control model to address these problems. A roadside infrastructure controller receives the states of all CAVs via vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication and sends control commands back to them. An attention-based observation encoder is designed where each vehicle can filter the relevant vehicle information from the global traffic state. The proposed model is evaluated in SUMO against three baselines: a model that observes only the neighbouring vehicles, a model that encodes the global traffic information, and the rule-based SUMO model. The results show that our model achieves the highest traffic flow, safety and smoothness. Furthermore, in a four-hour simulation with dynamic traffic demand, our model successfully avoids traffic jams, while other baseline models fail at high traffic flow. We also show that our model remains effective when human-driven vehicles are present. We further show that our model, trained in ideal communication conditions, can still remain collision-free and maintain throughput under realistic V2I communication errors. Finally, we visualise the relevance weights that an ego vehicle assigns to other vehicles in multiple traffic situations.

papers.abstract: Weighted split conformal prediction handles covariate shift by reweighting calibration scores with the likelihood ratio $v=dQ_X/dP_X$; its training-conditional coverage is a functional of the self-normalized weighted empirical distribution function $\hat F_m$, and we study the process $\sqrt m(\hat F_m-F_Q)$. It converges in $\ell^\infty$ to the Gaussian process $W(G(t))-F_Q(t)W(K^2)$, with $G(t)=\mathbb{E}_Q[v\mathbf{1}\{S\le t\}]$ and $K^2=1+χ^2(Q\|P)$, if and only if $χ^2(Q\|P)<\infty$ (for non-degenerate scores); $\sup v$ plays no role. The limit gives the joint law of the coverage across levels, consistent bootstraps, inflations asymptotically exact uniformly in the level, and Berry-Esseen-type rates. With estimated ratios, a uniform expansion remains valid when the estimate uses the calibration covariates; the estimation error enters through a covariance term that can reduce the variance below the oracle's, and a pairs bootstrap reproduces it. When the ratio is known, the weighted conformal threshold is semiparametrically efficient if and only if the ratio and the coverage indicator are uncorrelated under the test distribution, with an explicit efficient correction otherwise. When $χ^2(Q\|P)=\infty$, the ratio has a regularly varying tail of index $p\in(1,2)$ and the score decouples from it in the far tail, the finite-dimensional limits are $p$-stable at the rate $m^{1-1/p}$ up to a slowly varying factor.

papers.title: Diagnosis and Recovery in AI Workflows with Scarce Expert Capacity
papers.abstract: We study sequential decisions in AI workflows and other automated execution systems where failures of uncertain origin require recovery under limited shared expert capacity. Recovery choices affect future diagnostic demand, while expert availability changes which recovery actions are worthwhile. We coordinate diagnostic requests, expert dispatch, and checkpoint-based recovery to maximize expected net operating value. A finite-horizon model tracks uncertain error locations, remaining time, and shared expert capacity. Structural analysis shows how competition for diagnosis changes unaided recovery. When a full rebuild from checkpoint 0 is the best unaided fallback after failure, a larger expert pool can justify retaining more work despite a lower chance of immediate success. Capacity can also raise net operating value before fixed staffing costs while reducing diagnostic hours when advice is requested only after a failed trial. Our Diagnosis-Resource-Recovery Control (DRRC) policy coordinates these decisions through local recovery lookahead and estimates of service requirements and remaining time; its learning-augmented variant uses task-specific quality and duration estimates. In controlled simulations, larger pools draw more requests before repair, and selective diagnosis raises net value chiefly by reducing recovery costs. In a digital twin based on 177 software defects, DRRC with reference-assisted diagnosis increases mean timely completion by 3.27 percentage points and mean net value by 1.85% relative to automated recovery, although the net-value advantage remains uncertain across repositories. Expert capacity changes when workflows seek advice and how much work they preserve. Expansion may raise or lower diagnostic hours, so capacity and recovery design should be assessed jointly by their contribution to net operating value.

papers.title: PIRanNN: Random-Feature Pricing and Calibration under Jump-Diffusion and Stochastic-Volatility Models
papers.abstract: We study a random-feature method for pricing and calibrating European options under jump-diffusion (Merton, Kou) and stochastic-volatility (Heston, SABR) models. The network has one hidden layer with a probit activation and fixed random inner weights, so fitting it to the pricing equation, the payoff and the boundary conditions is a single regularised least-squares problem, with no iterative training. For Merton and Kou the jump integral of each feature is explicit, so no quadrature is needed. One factorisation of the least-squares matrix gives the price at every state and time, its Greeks, and the exact derivatives of the prices with respect to the model parameters for gradient-based calibration. For the jump models, subtracting the Black-Scholes price removes the payoff kink and reduces the pricing error by about two orders of magnitude. The method is then about as accurate as a standard Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme at the same run time, although a finite-difference scheme that also subtracts the Black-Scholes price is about two orders of magnitude more accurate still. On the test problems of a recent physics-informed neural network study, the method matches that network's accuracy in seconds instead of about half an hour. The calibration experiments show that a solver can fit the quotes and still return wrong parameters when its pricing error is not small compared with the effect of the parameters on the prices: without the subtraction the solver misses the jump parameters by up to 50%, and with it they are recovered to within 3%. For Heston and SABR, used as an applicability study with boundary conditions that need no reference prices, pricing errors are about one percent and the calibrated parameters are within about 15% of the true values.

papers.title: Recovery-Guided Model-Based Diffusion for Safety-Critical Legged Locomotion
papers.abstract: Safety-critical high-speed legged locomotion requires motion planners to balance safety foresight with online computational efficiency. Although short prediction horizons reduce rollout costs, they provide limited safety foresight, and strict safety constraints severely restrict the feasible trajectory space. We propose a recovery-guided model-based diffusion (MBD) framework for safety-critical legged locomotion. It incorporates a learned terminal recovery critic into short-horizon trajectory optimization. Specifically, the critic approximates the worst-case future clearance margin along rollouts of a designated recovery policy. We introduce a feasibility-guided refinement strategy that combines within-horizon constraints and terminal recoverability at each sampling stage, while retaining feasible elites to mitigate sampling-support loss. Across 50 paired randomized Unitree Go2 obstacle-avoidance trials, our approach achieves zero collisions and 98% strict-clearance success, while requiring substantially less computation than long-horizon MBD baselines. A project page is available at https://zack4417.github.io/rg-mbd/.

papers.title: Tight Sequential Confidence Intervals for Online Kernel Regression
papers.abstract: We characterize, in the worst case over kernels, the sharp minimax width of online confidence intervals for elements of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). This resolves the open problem posed by Vakili et al. (2021) in its original discrete-time form. A learner observes $y_i=f(x_i)+ε_i$ at adaptively chosen points, with $\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B$ and i.i.d. $R$-sub-Gaussian noise, and reports the interval $|f(x)-μ_n(x)|\leρ_n(δ)σ_n(x)$, where $μ_n$ and $σ_n$ are the posterior mean and standard deviation of a surrogate Gaussian process model with regularization parameter $λ$. Writing $ρ_n^*(δ)$ for the minimax confidence width for a fixed kernel, we show that, for the sum of a linear kernel and a periodic Sobolev kernel, all sufficiently large $n$, and all $δ\in(0,1/4]$, $ρ_n^*(δ)\asymp B+(R/λ)\sqrt{γ_n+\log(1/δ)}$, where $γ_n$ is the maximal information gain and grows polynomially in $n$. Building on Lattimore (2023), we construct an adaptive design on a fixed two-dimensional domain for which, under Gaussian noise, the normalized error at a prespecified point is $Ω(B+(R/λ)\sqrt{γ_n})$ with constant probability. This rules out the conjectured polylogarithmic width in the worst case over kernels and online designs.

papers.title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
papers.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

papers.title: Joint Learning of Factual and Counterfactual Worlds for Causal Prior-data Fitted Networks
papers.abstract: Estimating treatment effects is central to science across many disciplines and requires counterfactual reasoning about alternative worlds. In the real world, however, each unit reveals its outcome only under the factual world. Thus, the factual and counterfactual outcomes can never be jointly learned by any model trained on real data. The problem is therefore tractable only in synthetic settings, where both worlds can be generated. Recent progress on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) has shown that models pre-trained purely on synthetic data can transfer to real-world prediction. This paradigm has since carried over to causal effect estimation. Despite this fully synthetic setup, existing causal PFNs carry the real-world constraint into their training objective, confining learning to a single world's outcome per unit. The dependence between the two worlds is thereby lost, and the density of the treatment effect relies by default on independence, which is implausible in practice. We therefore propose joint learning, a training setup in which a causal PFN learns the joint distribution of the factual and counterfactual outcomes of each unit. From the joint distribution, we obtain both the response and the individual treatment effect densities, and at inference, we apply optimal transport across units to obtain an approximation of the average treatment effect density. Ours is therefore the first causal PFN approach to provide all three densities together while accounting for the cross-world dependence. We apply joint learning and optimal transport to existing causal PFNs and evaluate it across semi-synthetic, synthetic, and real benchmarks spanning diverse causal scenarios. The jointly trained models significantly improve upon their baselines in point estimation and uncertainty quantification in most settings, indicating that joint learning is a preferable training setup for causal PFNs.

papers.title: Physics-Grounded STL Monitoring from Image Observations
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation missions must satisfy timed and conditional requirements that can be expressed in signal temporal logic (STL). While a practical means of monitoring these requirements is from camera images, this is challenging because STL robustness depends on physical margins, such as distances and clearances, that are not directly observed. Rather than learning a separate visual monitor for each formula, we learn a shared latent representation from multi-view images and decode physically meaningful margins for individual predicates. Co-training the encoder with predicate decoders increases the certification rate from 58.7% to 96.3% compared with a frozen encoder, despite nearly unchanged predicate sign accuracy. STL semantics then compose these margins into robustness estimates for any bounded formula over the trained predicates, without retraining. We further calibrate the decoding errors of selected STL clauses using conformal prediction, yielding two-sided intervals that certify both satisfaction and violation and propagate through interval STL to any formula composed from the clauses. In simulated kitchen missions (LIBERO), our monitor correctly predicts satisfaction or violation in 98.9% of 4662 evaluations across 18 unseen formulas. For missions lasting up to 17 min, calibrated bounds establish satisfaction or violation for 96.9% of missions without incorrect conclusions. A single calibration also provides simultaneous 91.0% coverage across all 255 conjunctions of eight clauses, allowing new formulas without recalibration.

papers.title: Strategies for Constructing 3D Bioprinted Liver Organ Models
papers.abstract: Liver diseases are a severe global health challenge. Liver transplantation, as the gold-standard therapy for end stage liver disease, still suffers the fundamental constraint of severe donor shortage. 3D bioprinting technology provides new opportunities to construct functional liver organ model. Metabolic zonation is the core organizational principle of liver function, which is driven by gradients of oxygen and signaling molecules formed during the blood flow from the portal tract to the central vein. The existing in vitro model can not recapitulate this spatial heterogeneity, which severely limits the accuracy of drug metabolism research and toxicity prediction. In this article, the capability boundaries of four mainstream bioprinting technologies, i.e. extrusion-based, DLP photocuring, coaxial printing and embedded sacrificial material printing in reconstructing metabolic zonation are systematically reviewed. On this basis, the multi-technology collaborative strategy is proposed which starts from the target metabolic zonation map and works backward to match the technologies, and the three-layer architecture framework span from microscale topology to macroscale perfusion is constructed. This strategy provides the theoretic reference for advancing 3D bioprinted liver models from morphological biomimicry towards functional biomimicry. The future research may further verify the real efficacy of this framework in reproducing zone-dependent metabolism in in vitro pharmacological screening, and to explore the standardized application pathway in high-throughput system.

papers.abstract: This research aims to investigate the role of digital educational media in developing thinking and creativity skills among primary school children in Nigeria, in light of the rapid digital transformations in the education sector and the need to employ modern technologies to improve educational outcomes and develop learners' mental and creative abilities. The research problem stems from the gap between the potential offered by digital educational media and the level of their actual employment in Nigerian primary schools, which may negatively affect the development of higher-order thinking skills and creativity among children. The research seeks to identify the reality of using digital educational media in primary education in Nigeria, clarify their role in developing various thinking skills, reveal their contribution to enhancing creativity and innovation among pupils, and identify the main challenges facing their employment in the Nigerian educational environment. The research adopted the descriptive analytical method by analyzing educational literature, previous studies, and national documents related to digital education and digital culture in Nigeria. Studies confirm that interactive digital educational environments contribute to enhancing active learning, developing critical thinking and problem-solving skills, and stimulating creativity and innovation among learners. The study anticipates positive effects of digital educational media on developing thinking and creativity skills among primary school children, with effectiveness linked to appropriate technical infrastructure, teachers' competence in employing digital tools, and the availability of suitable digital educational resources. The study recommends developing digital infrastructure in primary schools, enhancing professional training programs for teachers, and systematically integrating digital educational media into curricula to prepare a generation capable of thinking, creating, and interacting with the requirements of the digital age.

papers.abstract: UHPC offers exceptionally high compressive strength but carries a heavy embodied-carbon footprint due to its elevated cement content, motivating the use of SCMs, including fly ash, silica fume, and GGBFS as partial cement replacements. However, accurate prediction remains challenging due to complex nonlinear interactions among the mixture constituents, fibre properties, curing conditions, and specimen geometry. Although existing ML studies capture these coupled effects and provide deterministic predictions, they often overlook uncertainty and heteroscedastic variability, leaving their reliability untested. This study developed an uncertainty-aware ML framework, using a harmonized database of 2,032 low-carbon UHPC mixtures incorporating one or more of FA, SF, and GGBFS, to predict compressive strength (23.6–––298 MPa) across curing ages of 1 to 90 days. In this paper, Physics-Embedded State-Space Operator Learning (PESO-Net) is proposed for multi-site, multi-horizon forecasting. The framework comprises a selective state-space encoder, gated cross-site mixing, a validation-controlled vertical shear regularizer, direct quantile decoding, and chronological conformal calibration. Observations from five years of 1-h synchronization at four anonymous sites were split chronologically into training, validation, calibration, and test sets, and one 168-h forecast trajectory was assessed over the 1–24 h, 1–72 h, and 1–168 h prefixes. The primary validation-weighted PESO-Net achieved MAE 2.080 m/s, RMSE 2.622 m/s, R² 0.176, 95.56% empirical coverage, 10.489 m/s mean interval width, and interval score 12.048. The primary validation-weighted PESO-Net had lower observed point errors and interval scores than the compared baselines. Among the four added model variants, PatchTST was closest by RMSE (2.727 m/s), with an interval score of 12.513. Mean predicted shear exponents ranged from 0.229 to 0.235, compared with observed means near 0.222; correlations of 0.287–0.302 support only limited physical agreement. The primary paired block-bootstrap RMSE contrast with Transformer was − 0.0185 m/s (95% CI − 0.0390 to 0.0042; p = 0.096), so statistical superiority was not established. papers.abstract: Abstract Fusion plasma control requires real-time coordination of multiple actuators under partial observations and model uncertainty. Here we demonstrate predictive control of a fusion plasma on the Large Helical Device using an adaptive digital-twin system that combines data assimilation with physics-based integrated modeling. The digital twin was dynamically synchronized with experimental observations, while heating and fueling inputs were optimized from its predictions to drive the plasma toward target states. Real-time adaptation and control estimation were performed on a remote supercomputer located approximately 1,000 km from the experimental device, using up to 10,000 CPU cores. These results establish a closed loop between an adaptive digital twin and a physical fusion plasma. They provide a route toward digital-twin-based control of fusion reactors and other partially observed complex systems.

papers.abstract: Probabilistic forecasts of Photovoltaic (PV) power are useful only if their intervals remain calibrated at new sites, in new seasons, and with the information available when forecasts are issued. This review asks whether AI models deliver such forecasts. Journal articles from 2022 to 2026 were retrieved from OpenAIRE and Crossref. A bibliometric map of 169 articles was combined with an abstract-level evidence map of 101 core studies, technical appraisal of eight full texts, and a structured synthesis of 13 matched proper-score contrasts. Output rose from 27 articles in 2022 to 66 in the partial year 2026, with conformal prediction and transfer learning appearing only from 2024 and foundation models in 2026. Among 77 core abstracts, 43% stated a horizon class or lead time, 22% a proper scoring rule, 34% interval coverage, 3% conditional coverage, 5% a new site or transfer, and none a tropical site. Within studies, AI models lowered the continuous ranked probability score or interval score against every comparator, by a median of 27% against the strongest baseline in the most complete study and by 12% to 13% in two others, always in-distribution. Only four of the eight appraised studies demonstrably used information available at issue time, and the only comparison with an operational day-ahead forecast favored the operational forecast. Wherever coverage was reported numerically by regime, nominal 90% intervals undercovered, falling to 76% in daylight hours. The evidence supports AI for more accurate PV forecast distributions in-distribution, not yet for calibrated and transferable forecasts under shift.

Output rose from 9 articles in 2022 and 2023 combined to 122 in the partial year 2026, spread across 122 sources. papers.abstract: In this paper, the fault-tolerant tracking problem is studied for parabolic PDE multi-agent systems with unknown distributed-parameter faults. A physics-informed neural network (PINN) reconstructs the states and faults from sparse interior measurements, and the learned control field is then applied without measurement updates. The goal is to relate the training loss of the PINN to the resulting tracking error. Under a rank condition on the sampled fault basis, the joint identifiability of the states and fault coefficients is established. Based on a Volterra observation equation, the independently evaluated losses are converted into fault and state error bounds, which yield an explicit tracking radius and transient over strongly connected directed graphs. These bounds provide conditions for comparing sensor placements, selecting a stopping loss and choosing the deployment duration. Numerical examples on a six-reactor network illustrate the results and identify the terms that dominate the a priori tracking radius.

papers.title: Two-Stage Supervisory MPC for Cooperative UAV Coverage with Fault-Triggered Mission Reconfiguration
papers.abstract: A two-stage supervisory model predictive control (MPC) framework is developed for cooperative unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) coverage during mission transit and reconfiguration after single-agent loss. A synchronized predictive supervisory layer coordinates sector responsibility and constrained motion planning through a ranked assignment–feasibility architecture: Stage 1 orders candidate sector assignments, and Stage 2 selects an assignment-consistent finite-horizon trajectory. This explicitly links combinatorial task allocation to predictive sensing-service constraints while separating mission coordination from low-level vehicle stabilization. Existence, exact-model interval-wise constraint satisfaction, and conditional post-fault solvability are characterized for the finite-dimensional analytical formulation. A fully specified, reproducible finite-control-library realization is assessed through matched-weight nominal ablations, continuous-time separation checks on executed first-order trajectories, and post-fault task-coverage histories. An additional controlled study tests assignment-conditioned trajectory candidates against frozen-task and universal-library references for five deterministic fault configurations, with matched pre-fault motion within each comparison. The experiments demonstrate a reproducible post-fault redistribution mechanism: candidate responsibilities are coupled to predictive service-feasibility tests, and the resulting motion choices are evaluated against coverage, overlap, terminal progress, and computation. papers.title: Multiscale simulation of oscillation in CO oxidation: From first principles to CFD based on reactive Bayesian force field
papers.abstract: Abstract Oscillations in CO oxidation over Pd catalysts represent a prototypical nonlinear phenomenon in heterogeneous catalysis, yet their underlying atomistic mechanisms and coupling with transport processes remain poorly understood, especially under nanoconfinement. Herein, the interfacial CO/O 2 oscillation confined within Pd interlayers was investigated under different conditions through molecular dynamics simulations (MD) complied with Bayesian reactive force field. A Bayesian interatomic potential was developed via a sparse Gaussian process (SGP) trained on datasets from an on‐the‐fly active learning strategy and AIMD simulations with high accuracy. MD analyses indicate that interlayer distance dominates the diffusion‐reaction equilibrium by regulating the spatial confinement effect. The CO/O 2 ratio modulates activity through competitive adsorption, with CO 2 yield optimized near the stoichiometric ratio (CO:O 2 ≈ 2:1). Incorporating SGP‐derived kinetics into continuum‐scale CFD models further confirms these trends at reactor scale. This work provides theoretical guidance for the design and optimization of nano‐confined catalytic materials.

papers.title: Compactness-Based Estimation of Sill-Controlled Hydraulic-Jump Parameters: Empirical Relationships and Physics-Informed Neural Modelling
papers.abstract: Estimating sill geometry and flow properties is essential for the preliminary design of stilling basins with compact sill-controlled hydraulic jumps. This study combines dimensional analysis, empirical regression, and physics-informed learning using 151 laboratory records from a horizontal rectangular channel, spanning inflow Froude numbers of 2.80–9.89 and compactness ratios of 0.893–2.217. Compactness, γ, is defined as the ratio of the calculated classical-jump roller length to the sill distance from the jump toe. Empirical relationships for relative sill height, S, relative sill position, X, and conjugate-depth ratio, Y, yield calibration R2 values of 0.980, 0.998, and 0.979, respectively. A cascaded physics-informed neural network with multi-head attention (C-PINN-MHA) provides complementary inference conditioned on γ. Under stratified five-fold cross-validation with globally normalized C7 loss scaling, R2 averaged 0.965 ± 0.005 for S and 0.982 ± 0.004 for Y, while the mean violation rate for the adopted one-sided specific-force criterion was 1.3 ± 1.6%. These results represent internal estimates of predictive performance under the stated normalization protocol. No violations of the same criterion occur on the fixed 37-record test set; however, satisfying this criterion alone does not establish the full momentum balance or hydraulic admissibility. Cumulative ablation indicates that the asymmetric feasibility penalty reduces violations, whereas subsequent architectural additions do not consistently improve accuracy. Because γ incorporates sill-position information, X is interpreted as a conditional reconstruction rather than an independent prediction. The empirical equations offer simple preliminary estimates, while the network makes hydraulic constraints explicit within its training objective.

papers.abstract: We investigate a physics-constrained neural network for reconstructing transient gas–liquid pipe flow under prescribed initial and boundary conditions. The method combines phase mass and mixture momentum equations with a horizontal drift-flux closure, bounded trainable corrections, and differentiable interpolation of SRK property tables. It uses temporal domain decomposition, a physics-loss schedule based on the training step, and a liquid-phase integral mass constraint. Training uses only the initial spatial profile, inlet gas and liquid mass-flow histories, and outlet pressure. Interior reference fields at positive times are reserved for post-training evaluation and are excluded from the loss and checkpoint selection. The baseline slug-flow case has overall methane/water feed mole fractions of 0.04/0.96. Its relative RMSEs are 0.64% for pressure, 3.52% for liquid velocity, 0.83% for gas void fraction, and 1.41% for gas velocity. The gas void fraction MAE is 0.0026. Gas compressibility and interphase slip influence the spatiotemporal evolution of the gas-phase variables. Additional slug, bubbly, and stratified-related cases are considered to assess reconstruction across flow states. All six cases are trained independently for 20,000 optimization steps.

papers.title: Four-Dimensional Smart Biomaterials in Dentistry: Dynamic Shape-Morphing Materials for Adaptive Dental Restoration and Regeneration. A Narrative Review: Review Article
papers.abstract: Conventional dental restorative materials are structurally static and cannot adapt to the continuously changing biological and mechanical conditions of the oral cavity, a limitation contributing to microleakage, interfacial degradation, and restoration failure. Four-dimensional (4D) biomaterials, fabricated from stimulus-responsive materials that undergo programmed transformation over time, have been proposed to address this constraint. This narrative review examined their mechanisms and applications across restorative dentistry, orthodontics, prosthodontics, implantology, and guided bone regeneration, searching PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for reviews, in vitro studies, preclinical work, and clinical reports published principally within the last five years. Thermoresponsive shape-memory polymers have progressed furthest toward clinical use, with direct-printed aligners delivering forces of 0.3 to 1.7 N within the intraoral temperature range. Porous shape-memory scaffolds achieve shape recovery ratios above ninety per cent and compressive moduli comparable with trabecular bone, and preclinical models demonstrate self-fitting adaptation to irregular defects alongside vascularized bone ingrowth. Evidence in implantology, prosthodontics, and regenerative applications nonetheless remains predominantly preclinical, and no long-term randomized data exist for any 4D dental application. Equipment costs, absent testing standards, and regulatory frameworks built for materials with fixed properties remain the principal barriers to translation.

papers.title: The The Effect of the POGIL Model on Student Learning Outcomes in Terms of Students’ Mathematical Self-Efficacy
papers.abstract: Mathematical self-efficacy is a critical affective factor in mathematics learning: students with low self-efficacy tend to give up more easily when facing mathematical difficulties, yet how the benefits of active learning models are distributed across students with different self-efficacy levels within the same classroom remains underexamined. This study aims to determine the effect of the Process Oriented Guided Inquiry Learning (POGIL) model on student learning outcomes and to analyze differences in student learning outcomes across mathematical self-efficacy categories (low, moderate, high). This best-practice study used a quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design, involving 36 tenth-grade students of SMA Negeri 3 Salatiga on the topic of Exponents and Logarithms. Data were collected through a learning outcome test and a mathematical self-efficacy questionnaire, then analyzed using a paired-samples t-test and a one-way ANOVA followed by a Games-Howell post-hoc test, at a significance level of α = 0.05. The results showed that the POGIL model had a significant effect on student learning outcomes (t = -5.920; sig. = 0.000). In addition, a significant difference in learning outcomes (posttest) was found among the self-efficacy categories (F = 17.650; sig. = 0.000), with mean scores increasing consistently by category: low = 40.50; moderate = 69.76; high = 90.80. As an additional analysis, a consistent pattern of improvement (N-Gain) was also found across self-efficacy categories (low = 0.02; moderate = 0.44; high = 0.80). This study concludes that the POGIL model is effective for student learning outcomes, with both achievement and the magnitude of improvement influenced by students' levels of mathematical self-efficacy. Teachers are recommended to pair the POGIL model with deliberate scaffolding for students with low self-efficacy, and future research is encouraged to examine POGIL's longer-term effect on self-efficacy itself using designs that include a control group and a more balanced sample across self-efficacy categories.

papers.title: [Early effectiveness of patient-specific three-dimensional-printed porous tantalum blocks for hip revision in patients with Paprosky type
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the early clinical and radiographic outcomes of patient-specific three-dimensional-printed porous tantalum blocks for the reconstruction of Paprosky type Ⅲ massive acetabular bone defects in hip revision. METHODS: The clinical data of 17 patients (17 hips) with Paprosky type Ⅲ massive acetabular bone defects undergoing revision after hip arthroplasty between January 2022 and January 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The cohort comprised 6 males and 11 females, with a mean age of 59.4 years (range, 37-80 years). Nine patients had Paprosky type ⅢA defects and 8 had type ⅢB defects, including 5 with pelvic discontinuity. All patients underwent acetabular side (9 cases) or both acetabular and femoral components (8 cases) reconstruction with patient-specific three-dimensional-printed porous tantalum blocks combined with revision acetabular cups. Harris hip score (HHS) and visual analogue scale (VAS) score were compared between preoperative and last follow-up. The position of radiographic hip center of rotation (rCOR), acetabular cup inclination and anteversion, osseointegration, and implant stability were evaluated by anteroposterior pelvic X-ray films and CT, and perioperative complications and re-revision were recorded. RESULTS: The operation was successfully completed in all patients, with a mean operation time of 141.2 minutes (range, 80-280 minutes) and a mean intraoperative blood loss of 752.9 mL (range, 300-1 500 mL). All patients completed follow-up, with a mean duration of 22.1 months (range, 13-41 months). At last follow-up, the HHS score significantly increased from 37.0±5.8 to 87.9±3.0, while the VAS score significantly decreased from 6.0 (5.5, 7.0) to 0.0 (0.0, 1.0) (P<0.05). The horizontal rCOR distance on the operated side improved significantly when compared with the preoperative value (P<0.05) and did not differ significantly from that on the contralateral side (P>0.05). The vertical rCOR distance decreased significantly (P<0.05) but remained greater than that on the contralateral side (P<0.05). At last follow-up, all acetabular reconstructions remained radiographically stable, with an acetabular cup inclination of (41.87±4.38)° and an acetabular cup anteversion of (19.47±3.77)°. No intraoperative screw penetration through the inner pelvic cortex or neurovascular injury was recorded. No heterotopic ossification, clinically significant limb-length discrepancy, implant mismatch requiring additional adjustment or component replacement, tantalum blocks migration, screw loosening or breakage, or aseptic loosening was observed. Postoperative venous thrombosis occurred in 2 patients, both of whom improved following treatment. No other major complication was reported. CONCLUSION: Patient-specific three-dimensional-printed porous tantalum blocks demonstrated favorable early clinical and radiographic outcomes in the reconstruction of Paprosky type Ⅲ massive acetabular bone defects, with improvements in hip function, pain relief, radiographic stability, and restoration of the hip center of rotation. Larger multicenter and random clinical trials with longer follow-up are warranted to establish long-term outcomes and potential advantages over alternative reconstruction techniques.

papers.title: [Mid- to long-term effectiveness of personalized three-dimensional-printed microporous titanium-coated total wrist arthroplasty for advanced wrist diseases].
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the mid- to long-term effectiveness of personalized three-dimensional (3D)-printed microporous titanium-coated total wrist arthroplasty for advanced wrist diseases. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted of the clinical data of 15 patients with advanced wrist diseases who underwent personalized 3D-printed microporous titanium-coated total wrist arthroplasty between February 2019 and March 2026 and were followed up more than 5 years. The cohort included 8 males and 7 females, aged 21-69 years, with a mean age of 42.4 years. The underlying conditions included rheumatoid arthritis of the wrist in 8 cases, osteoarthritis of the wrist in 5 cases, post-traumatic wrist deformity with fusion in 1 case, and an open partial wrist defect caused by a gunshot injury in 1 case. Visual analogue scale (VAS) score for pain, wrist range of motion (flexion, extension, ulnar deviation, radial deviation, forearm pronation, and supination), and grip strength were compared between the early- to mid-term postoperative assessment (12-46 months postoperatively) and last follow-up. At last follow-up, X-ray films and CT scans were obtained to evaluate prosthesis loosening using the Wrightington radiographic loosening classification, as well as osseointegration and prosthesis stability. RESULTS: All 15 patients completed follow-up, with a duration of 5-7 years (mean, 5.98 years). Compared with the early- to mid-term postoperative assessment, VAS scores decreased significantly and grip strength increased significantly at last follow-up (P<0.05). No significant difference was observed in wrist flexion, extension, ulnar deviation, radial deviation, forearm pronation, or supination (P>0.05). X-ray films showed satisfactory alignment of the radial and carpal components, without obvious prosthesis subsidence, migration, fracture, dislocation, or periprosthetic fracture. CT scans demonstrated continuous bone surrounding the radial and carpal stems, with good bone ingrowth into the microporous titanium-coated regions and no continuous radiolucent lines, obvious osteolysis, or periprosthetic bone resorption. According to the Wrightington radiographic loosening classification, none of the 15 patients showed radiolucency in three or more zones around either the radial component (5 zones) or the carpal component (6 zones), and none met the criteria for prosthesis loosening. CONCLUSION: Personalized 3D-printed microporous titanium-coated total wrist arthroplasty demonstrates satisfactory mid- to long-term outcomes in the treatment of advanced wrist diseases. At more than 5 years postoperatively, patients experienced further pain relief and increased grip strength, while wrist range of motion remained generally stable. The prostheses demonstrated favorable mid- to long-term stability.

papers.title: Sequential active learning incorporating multi-objective optimization for selective bacterial growth
papers.abstract: Developing selective media for bacterial cultivation is challenging because of complex nutritional requirements and the need to suppress competing species. Here, we present a machine learning-based sequential active learning framework that incorporates multi-objective optimization to design selective media from 30 common components for six phylogenetically diverse bacteria. High-throughput monoculture growth assays generated data used to train gradient-boosting decision tree models with multi-objective functions, which predicted media formulations that maximize target growth while minimizing non-target growth. Iterative cycles of prediction and experimental validation refined media compositions, yielding selective media that enhanced target bacterial growth and selectivity. Coculture experiments confirmed the effectiveness of the selective media in promoting specific bacteria within communities, demonstrating that monoculture data can predict community growth dynamics. This data-driven approach enables selective medium development without prior knowledge of bacterial physiology or inhibitors, providing a scalable and systematic framework for microbiology and systems biology applications.

papers.title: Interactive methods of mine safety education in educational institutions
papers.abstract: This article provides a theoretical and methodological examination of interactive approaches to mine safety education in general secondary and higher educational institutions in Ukraine. The problem is approached as a matter of developing reliable safe decision-making rather than memorising the appearance of explosive objects. The purpose is to systematise interactive teaching approaches and to construct a feasible educational model aligned with the principles of explosive ordnance risk education (EORE). The materials include the international mine action standard IMAS 12.10, UNICEF risk education resources and published systematic reviews and meta-analyses of active learning, serious games, problem-based learning, simulations and formative feedback. The article distinguishes evidence from general educational settings from the still untested transfer of those effects to mine safety instruction. A teaching framework is developed around four complementary learning functions: recognising danger signals without approaching suspicious items, choosing protective behaviour, communicating risk and transferring learned responses to unfamiliar scenarios. Interactive techniques include facilitated case discussion, illustrated non-realistic cards, branching digital scenarios, role-based communication exercises, collaborative decision tasks and feedback-supported retrieval practice. A matrix connects learning objectives, instructional activities, observed learner responses and assessment indicators. Particular attention is paid to the ethical and psychological boundaries of instruction. Exercises must not expose participants to genuine or unidentified objects, recreate explosive incidents or teach the handling, movement or neutralisation of explosive ordnance. The proposed instructional sequence is presented as a design framework, not as an intervention whose effectiveness has already been empirically demonstrated. Recommended evaluation procedures include baseline and delayed assessment, observation of choices within safe hypothetical situations, age-adapted feedback and confidential treatment of participant data. The proposed model may support teachers and educational administrators in planning consistent and safe lessons; however, further field validation is required to assess its impact across learners, age groups, locations and learning formats.

papers.title: Towards reduced stress shielding: experimental evaluation of additively manufactured topology-optimised porous hip implants
papers.abstract: Topology-optimised porous hip implants are intended to tailor load transfer and potentially mitigate stress shielding, but the mechanical response of manufactured designs may differ from computational predictions. This study evaluated Ti6Al4V-Gr23 hip implants derived from a previously published modified floating projection topology optimisation design and manufactured by laser powder bed fusion. Four stem and six neck specimens underwent quasi-static compression in plaster-supported fixtures; two additional specimens per configuration underwent cyclic loading informed by ISO 7206–4 and ISO 7206–6. Mean actuator-derived apparent construct secant stiffness was 1.6846 ± 0.0634 kN/mm for the stem and 1.8626 ± 0.0628 kN/mm for the neck. These values exceeded previous finite element predictions by 32.8% and 46.8%, respectively, although the measurement definitions and boundary conditions were not equivalent. Both stem fatigue specimens completed 5 million cycles (100–2,300 N), and both neck specimens completed 1 million cycles (100–5,340 N), without observed macroscopic failure. Enclosed head cavities required corrective powder removal and local repair. The findings characterise condition-specific mechanical performance and manufacturing challenges; reduced stress shielding was not experimentally established.

papers.title: Bayesian Optimization for Tuning Nonlinear Predictive Control of an Acetone Purification Column
papers.abstract: A Bayesian optimization method is developed to tune predictive control for an acetone purification column operating in a high-purity region. Aspen Dynamics is coupled with MATLAB through OPC DA. With the reboiler duty fixed, reflux flow is manipulated using an incremental ridge regression model identified from 20 historical trajectories in logarithmic impurity coordinates. A nonlinear inverse transformation provides overhead composition predictions. The inner controller optimizes three move blocks subject to magnitude and rate limits, while an outer Gaussian process and expected improvement criterion select the move penalty with post-run purity-margin screening. Fifteen valid co-simulation runs include relative feed-flow change up to ±0.1% and relative feed-acetone mole-fraction decrease up to 0.1%. In the negative-flow confirmation run, the frozen penalty value of 0.01 has a minimum overhead acetone mole fraction value of 0.999004900 and causes a 22.41% reduction in the fixed performance score value relative to the mean of two runs with an original penalty value of 0.05. All valid samples from the three frozen-parameter confirmation runs meet the 0.999 criterion; but too much purity still remains when faced with the positive-flow disturbance. These results indicate sampled product-quality satisfaction and higher aggregate performance in the negative-flow case, within the local disturbance range and operating limits investigated here.
